points.description: States that the compiler inserts a copy of the function's code (its body) in place of the call, so the function's code is duplicated rather than jumped to. Equivalent wording such as 'the function body is substituted/expanded inline' earns the mark.

States that this copying happens at every place where the function is called (every call site), so each call gets its own copy. Equivalent wording such as 'each occurrence of the call is replaced' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for an answer that says the compiler copies the function's code and that this is done at every place the function is called. Award P1 for the copying of the code and P2 for the every-call-site idea; an answer with only one of these gets the corresponding marks. No partial credit is needed since each point is a single clear idea.
